solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brown’s hedging because of Mark’s heartless character

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so the colour word wraps round what follows

blocks.note: tan is a light brown colour
in, as in 'in view of', can mean on account of
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown is being evasive on account of a heartless person named Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' and 'Mark' look like people's names; both are just letter sources.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Man in The Wizard of Oz is the figure who lacks a heart and goes to the wizard to get one.

clue.text: Fellow starts to bellyache over love arguing it involves the luck of the draw

definitions.text: it involves the luck of the draw

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, so only the first letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: Tom is a stock name for any man or male
the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A man begins grumbling about a lovers' quarrel that comes down to chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle where tickets are pulled from a drum, so winning depends on chance in the draw.

clue.text: Without feeling before carrying on with first lieutenant

indicators.note: what carries something holds it, so the word for before takes the next words inside

blocks.note: numb means unable to feel
ere is a poetic word for before
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer carries on with his duties without any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' looks like one phrase meaning continuing, but 'carrying' is the container signal and 'on' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy, Number One is the informal title of the first lieutenant, the captain's second in command.

clue.text: Having a strong dislike of American poetry

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone who simply cannot stand American poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To be averse to something is to be opposed to it or have a firm distaste for it.

clue.text: Rude to stuff fairy queen back in carriage

indicators.note: going back means the name is read from its end to its start
stuffing puts filling inside, so the word for rude goes into the middle

blocks.note: rough means coarse or unrefined
Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, named in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A vulgar suggestion about cramming a fairy queen into the back of a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Mab is the fairy queen whom Mercutio describes in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn closed carriage, named after Lord Brougham.

clue.text: Right about priestess’s loose living

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation for right surrounds the next name

blocks.note: RT is the abbreviation for right
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A judgement about a priestess who is leading a dissolute life.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on priestess does no work beyond joining the parts; Io was a priestess of Hera loved by Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot in an old sense means wild, dissipated revelry or debauchery, as in 'riotous living'.

clue.text: Upper class newspaper boss maintains no writer is barred

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so the outer letters keep the next words within them

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper class
taken as written
a pen is a writing instrument
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A posh editor insists that no journalist is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The upper-class letter and the editor together form the outside, so the container is split across the start and end of the clue's first phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is barred stays shut, and something unopened remains closed.

clue.text: Pure cocaine’s cut to produce speed

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the drug's abbreviation is taken away

blocks.note: chaste means pure, untainted
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug-dealer's tale: uncut cocaine is diluted to make amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: CHASTE loses its C to leave HASTE. 'Speed' in the surface is the drug; in the definition it is quickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is rapidity of movement or action, the same as hurry or quickness.

clue.text: A few said to be upset by smell coming from horse

indicators.note: said points to how the words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a few means some, which is said the same as sum
a tang is a sharp smell or taste

explanation.surface: Some people are put off by the odour that comes off a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the sound-alike word is read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a small wild or semi-wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: Actor‘s mother joins revolutionary group

indicators.note: joining puts one piece directly after the other
a revolution turns things round, so the band's name is read backwards

blocks.note: mum is a British word for mother
REM is the American rock band

explanation.surface: A performer's mother signs up with a band of rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary group' reads as rebels, but the group is the rock band, and revolutionary turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mummer is an actor in a traditional masked mime or folk play, so it is a performer on a stage.

clue.text: It’s big for Cuba to have succeeded after withdrawal of American bid

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a huge thing, not a dictionary synonym

indicators.note: withdrawing is drawing back, so these letters run backwards
after places the letter for succeeded at the end, behind the turned letters

blocks.note: C is Cuba's international vehicle registration code
US is short for American
in solo whist, a solo is a bid to win five tricks alone
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: It would be quite something for Cuba to win once the United States abandons its offer.
explanation.walkthrough: C, then US SOLO turned back (OLOSSU), then S. The surface pretends to be political news; every word is a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a statue or person of enormous size, like the Colossus of Rhodes, so it is something huge.

clue.text: In time money fills container

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so the first pieces sit within the container

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
tin is old slang for money
a bag is a container

explanation.surface: Eventually cash goes into a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition, but it is the cricketing adjective; tin is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the side that is in is the side currently batting, as opposed to fielding.

clue.text: Supervises broadcast from abroad

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so it is the sound of the word that matters

blocks.note: oversees means supervises

explanation.surface: Someone manages a programme transmitted from another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas, used as an adjective, describes things coming from or relating to foreign countries.

clue.text: Scene tampered with by amateur playwright

indicators.note: something tampered with has been interfered with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
A is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: A dramatist's scene is spoiled by an untrained meddler.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Roman Stoic philosopher who also wrote tragedies, so he was a dramatist.

clue.text: Extremely lively after lawyer gets to the point

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, the first and last
after puts the selected letters at the end, behind the lawyer

blocks.note: a brief is informal for a barrister or lawyer
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A very energetic barrister comes straight to the heart of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIEF then LY. A brief is British slang for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking briefly means saying things concisely and without digression, which is speaking succinctly.

clue.text: Excited to find work in the centre of Prague

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the middle two letters of the city are kept
in tells us the word for work goes inside those kept letters

blocks.note: the middle two letters of the city's name
to go is to work or function, as of a machine

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at landing a job in central Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the centre of Prague' looks like one location phrase; 'in' places the work inside, and 'the centre of' picks the city's middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, full of excitement and curiosity.

clue.text: Shakespeare’s tailor‘s grave isn’t left untidy

indicators.note: untidy means messed up, so the letters are put into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The Bard's tailor's burial place has not been kept tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'grave' a tomb; it is just letters to rearrange with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Starveling is the tailor among the rustic mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Flawed politician involved in fierce struggles with Tory leader

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
being involved in something means being caught up inside it
the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is used
with means alongside, so the letter is added on at the end

blocks.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written for rearranging
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A faulty MP gets caught up in bitter fights alongside the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician sits inside the rearranged letters, not at their edge, so the anagram must be settled before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperfect means having faults or defects, not complete or without blemish.

clue.text: Is breaking spell a divinely conferred talent?

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: a charm is a magic spell
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether interrupting an enchantment is a God-given gift.
explanation.walkthrough: IS breaks into CHARM, then A. 'a' does double duty in the surface as part of the definition phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology charisma is a gift of grace from God; it now means personal magnetism, a natural gift.

clue.text: Equalised without assistance – just

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: evened means made equal
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Someone drew level in a game unaided, and fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside, its old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An even-handed person treats everyone fairly and impartially, which is what being just means.

clue.text: Without right to speak boldly

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend
a claim is a right or entitlement to something

explanation.surface: Having no entitlement to address people forthrightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly and loudly, voicing something with force or emotion.

clue.text: Jet falling short of railway siding

indicators.note: falling short means stopping before the end, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: a spurt is a sudden jet of liquid

explanation.surface: An aircraft that crashes before it reaches a branch line.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURT loses its final T. 'Jet' suggests an aeroplane; it is a squirt of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a short branch line of railway leading off the main track.

clue.text: Enlisted soldiers crossing river on the way back to Germany and home

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the river's name is read backwards
crossing something means straddling it, so the soldiers sit around it
to means added on, so the remaining pieces follow

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the Po is the longest river in Italy
D is Germany's international vehicle code, from Deutschland
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Troops crossing a river on their return to Germany and their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British army corps; the Po is Italy's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roped in is to be persuaded to take part, so it means being recruited or signed up.

clue.text: In court to continue getting maintenance

blocks.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court
to keep on means to continue

explanation.surface: A divorcing spouse goes to court to keep receiving financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface maintenance is alimony; in the answer it is looking after property.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair, which is its maintenance.

clue.text: Poison dog over time

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for time runs the other way

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone poisons a dog repeatedly over time.
explanation.walkthrough: CUR then ERA turned over, ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract used by South American hunters on arrow tips, which paralyses its victim.

clue.text: Supports Settle school’s head

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: to settle is to come to rest
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A headteacher props up a school in Settle, the Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: REST then S. Settle is also a market town in North Yorkshire, which the capital letter exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rests as a noun are props or stands, things that hold something up.

clue.text: Nonsense to applaud Republican during strike

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the party letter sits inside

blocks.note: to clap is to applaud
to tap is to strike lightly
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: It's absurd to cheer a Republican in the middle of a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action; it means hit lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious, empty talk meant to win applause, so it is rubbish.

clue.text: Good to have the Queen’s support

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, hence good
ER is Elizabeth Regina; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: It is good to have Her Majesty behind you.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is an upright pillar holding up an arch or bridge span, so it is a structural prop.

clue.text: Fool wrong to assume arsenic’s a killer

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the chemical symbol is taken inside

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A dimwit is wrong to suppose arsenic is lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assume' looks like suppose, but it means take on, the container signal; the 's after arsenic is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is someone who murders a prominent person, usually for hire or politics.

clue.text: Worm turning contributes to bloodier encounter

indicators.note: contributing to something means being part of it, so the letters lie within the words
turning round means the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A downtrodden person fighting back adds to a more violent clash.
explanation.walkthrough: The worm turning is the idiom for a meek person retaliating; here 'Worm' is the definition and 'turning' reverses DIEREN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nereid is a marine polychaete worm such as the ragworm, named after the sea nymphs of myth.

clue.text: Overwhelming defeat as Cram’s resilience finally cracked

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
something cracked is broken, so the letters are broken up and reset

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A rout in which the runner Steve Cram's stamina at last gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram is a British middle-distance runner of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, a massacre is an informal word for a crushing, one-sided defeat.

clue.text: Excellent tenor packs club

indicators.note: packing something means holding it within, so the club takes the voice letter inside

blocks.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A fine tenor singer joins a club.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SPOON. 'Club' suggests a society; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is British informal for exactly right or perfect.
